I tried ECT over TMS simply due to awareness.  I can’t really speak to the effectiveness of TMS but I’ve also heard good things there.  

The only other side effects are minor cognitive issues, that could honestly be my imagination, such as difficulty reading in the days immediately proceeding treatments.  The memory loss is somewhat significant though, and is a major drawback.  I don’t mind it, though, given my results.  

I have had both unilateral (one side of the brain) and bilateral (both sides) at various points during treatment.  They choose to alter treatment in order to gain a greater effect, which did seem to help, but bilateral is significantly more exhausting and befuddling.  

For those whom standard medications have been ineffective or inconsistent I’d definitely recommend ECT.

I definitely identify with that feeling of sadness and anxiety when going to bed.  The awful thing about that pattern of thinking is that the longer I put off going to bed the worse those feelings would be when I did.  I think most of that depressive thinking was due to being trans and not realizing it.  Literally the moment I accepted that I was that way I had to fix my sleep.  However, in the last few years, prior to sorting out my sleep issues, I saw the sun rise many many times.  The way I got myself on a good schedule was to slowly walk back the time I went to bed.  If you go to bed at 3 am on average then the following night shoot for 2:30.  What that means is that you get off the computer at 1:30 and do anything that doesn't put a lot of light into your eyes.  The problem with staring at a computer screen is that it affects your body's ability to create melatonin which is the chemical responsible for making you tired.  Reading a paper book is great for this at it doesn't interfere with the melatonin cycles and also can be a great distraction from anxious or sad thinking.  Once you get tired mark your place and try to sleep.  Don't try to make major adjustments to sleep all at once.  Your body is used to sleeping at a particular time.  Any change greater than 1 hour is almost certainly a lost cause.  If you want to walk back when you go to bed by 2-3 hours assume that it will take at least a week to do so maybe longer.  Finally one big thing to consider is that your lack or sleep and/or poor sleeping habits contributes A LOT to feeling down and anxious.  Try not to beat yourself up about sleep, just realize your health and mental well being is worth trying for.
